newsitem.title: GERMANY: Wall St highs spark modest gains on German DAX.
newsitem.headline: Wall St highs spark modest gains on German DAX.

text.p: German shares notched up modest gains in bourse trade on Wednesday, as the market drew some strength from overnight gains on Wall Street and placed uncertainty about monetary union on the backburner.
The blue chip DAX index advanced 12.42 points, or 0.34 percent, to close the floor session at 3,677.43 points.

The stable dollar underpinned the gains but dealers noted that volumes remained low and sentiment was markedly tentative, especially given that the Dow Jones index had hit its third consecutive record on Tuesday.
"We won't do much more here until the Amsterdam Summit," said one dealer. "I think we can forget about records for now."

European Union leaders are expected to pin down a final agreement on the stability pact -- a crucial pact designed to ensure budgetary rigour under monetary union -- at the Amsterdam meeting on March 16 and 17.
But many German market players remain nervous that France will refuse to play ball on the stability pact, after the new French Socialist government said it needed more time to reflect on the deal.

There were few outstanding moves on the market, barring a continued technically-driven rise in Deutsche Telekom shares and fresh interest in retailer Karstadt amid renewed talk that a large stake in the firm was poised to change hands.
Although WCM, the firm pinpointed as the buyer for a Karstadt stake, once again denied any such plans, Karstadt shares rose 25 marks, or four percent to 635 marks.
Telekom ended the day up 50 pfennigs, or 1.2 percent, at 41.50 marks amid relatively healthy volumes.
The approach of a major options expiry deadline next week also capped broader price gains, dealers said.
Futures and options dealers on Germany's DTB futures exchange often act to influence prices on the cash market as an expiry deadline looms.
